correctness.rationale: For P(1^r,a,b), r≥2, d=b-a, the a- and b-chart nonidentity ages have integer numerators rk+[kd]_a and rk+[-kd]_b. Solving equality to the respective modulus on the canonical nonterminal boundary d=r or a=r+d yields, on d=r, j_b=1+floor(a/r) and j_a nonzero only at a=r (one) and 2r (two). On a=r+d, 0≤d<r, the a-chart contributes one junior; the b-chart contributes one only if d=0. These disjoint components have 2r and r pairs; their J histogram is J=1:2r-2, J=2:r, J=3:1 and J=5:1, hence sum 4r+6. The r=2 endpoint and d=0 (equal heavy weights) are handled explicitly. The pre-existing canonical triangle is an external input, independently checked in bounded cases; the all-r junior count follows from modular case splits, not finite extrapolation.
